info.title: Strapi CMS REST API
info.description:
The REST API exposed by any self-hosted or Strapi Cloud instance of Strapi 5, the open-source headless CMS.

This specification describes the *generic* Strapi 5 REST surface. Strapi is a headless CMS in which content types are defined by the developer of each individual instance, so the resource segment of each route is a variable, not a fixed name:

- **Collection types** are addressed by their plural API ID, e.g. `/api/articles`, `/api/products`. They support list, create, read-one, update and delete.
- **Single types** are addressed by their singular API ID, e.g. `/api/homepage`, `/api/global-setting`. There is only ever one document, so they support read, update and delete — but not list or create.

Because both forms occupy the same position in the path, they are described here by the shared `{apiId}` path parameter. Substitute the plural API ID of a collection type, or the singular API ID of a single type, as documented per operation.

## Documents and documentId

Strapi 5 replaced Strapi 4's numeric entry `id` with a `documentId`: an opaque string that identifies a *document* — the set of all variations of an entry across locales and across its draft and published versions. All collection-type item routes are keyed by `documentId`. A numeric `id` is still returned for backwards compatibility, but it identifies a single underlying database row rather than the document, and should not be used to address entries. The Upload plugin is the exception: its routes are still keyed by the numeric file `id`.

## Response shape

Every content response is wrapped in `data` and `meta`. Strapi 5 flattened the response compared to Strapi 4 — fields now appear directly on the document rather than nested under an `attributes` object.

## Draft & Publish caveats

The `status` query parameter selects the draft or published version and is well defined for read operations. Its behaviour on **create and update is not**, and there are long-standing open bugs:

- Documents created through the REST API are auto-published even when `status=draft` is supplied ([strapi/strapi#21544](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/21544), [#24860](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/24860), [#23196](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/23196)).
- Updating an entry publishes it, with no REST route to unpublish it again ([strapi/strapi#24547](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/24547)).

Setting `publishedAt: null` to force a draft is deprecated in Strapi 5 and does not reliably work either. There are no built-in REST publish/unpublish routes; publishing state is authoritative only through the Document Service API in server-side code, or the admin panel. Instances that need REST-driven publish/unpublish typically add custom controllers, which are outside the scope of this specification.

A client that must guarantee draft creation should verify `publishedAt` on the response and take corrective action rather than assume `status=draft` was honoured.

servers.description: A Strapi instance. Strapi is self-hosted or run on Strapi Cloud, so the host is specific to each deployment. The API is served under the /api prefix by default; this can be changed via the `rest.prefix` setting in config/api.js.

baseUrl.description: Origin of the Strapi instance, e.g. http://localhost:1337 for a local development server, or https://your-project.strapiapp.com on Strapi Cloud.

tags.name: Collection types
tags.description: Content types that hold many documents, addressed by their plural API ID.

tags.name: Single types
tags.description: Content types that hold exactly one document, addressed by their singular API ID.

tags.name: Upload
tags.description: The Upload plugin, which backs Strapi's Media Library.

get.summary: List documents in a collection type, or get a single type
get.description:
For a **collection type** (plural API ID, e.g. `articles`) this returns a paginated list of documents, and `meta.pagination` is populated.

For a **single type** (singular API ID, e.g. `homepage`) this returns the one document, and `data` is an object rather than an array.

Only published versions are returned unless `status=draft` is supplied.

200.description: A list of documents (collection type) or a single document (single type).

post.summary: Create a document in a collection type
post.description:
Creates a new document in the collection type identified by its plural API ID. Not applicable to single types, which are created implicitly by a PUT.

The payload must be wrapped in a `data` object. Fields not defined on the content type are silently ignored.

See the Draft & Publish caveats in the API description: on instances with Draft & Publish enabled, documents created through this route are known to be auto-published regardless of the `status` parameter. Verify `publishedAt` on the response rather than assuming a draft was created.

put.description:
Updates the single type identified by its singular API ID. If the single type does not yet have a document, one is created.

For collection types, use `PUT /{apiId}/{documentId}` instead.

delete.description:
Deletes the document held by the single type identified by its singular API ID.

For collection types, use `DELETE /{apiId}/{documentId}` instead.

get.summary: Get one document from a collection type
get.description: Returns a single document by its `documentId`. Only the published version is returned unless `status=draft` is supplied.

put.summary: Update a document in a collection type
put.description:
Updates the document identified by `documentId`. Only the fields present in the payload are modified; omitted fields are left untouched.

See the Draft & Publish caveats in the API description: updating a document is known to publish it, and there is no REST route to unpublish it again.

delete.summary: Delete a document from a collection type
delete.description: Deletes the document identified by `documentId`, including all of its locale and draft/published variations.

post.summary: Upload files to the Media Library
post.description:
Uploads one or more files. The request must be `multipart/form-data`.

Files can optionally be attached to an entry in the same request by supplying `ref` (the content type UID, e.g. `api::article.article`), `refId` (the entry id) and `field` (the media attribute name on that content type).

Supplying the `id` query parameter instead updates the metadata of an existing file rather than uploading a new one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: When supplied, updates the `fileInfo` of the existing file with this id instead of creating a new one.

files.description: One or more files to upload.

fileInfo.description: JSON-encoded metadata for the uploaded file: `name`, `alternativeText` and `caption`.

ref.description: UID of the content type to attach the file to, e.g. `api::article.article`.

refId.description: Id of the entry to attach the file to. Required when `ref` is supplied.

field.description: Name of the media attribute on the target content type. Required when `ref` is supplied.

path.description: Optional destination folder, used by providers that support it.

413.description: Payload too large — the file exceeds the instance's configured size limit.

get.summary: List files in the Media Library
get.description: Returns all files. Unlike content routes, this returns a bare array rather than a `data`/`meta` envelope. Use `/upload/files/page` for a paginated response.

200.description: The files in the Media Library.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric id of the file. Note that the Upload plugin is keyed by numeric id, not by `documentId`.

get.description: Returns a single file from the Media Library by its numeric id. This is the id carried by media fields on documents, so it is the value to look up after populating a media relation.

delete.description: Removes the file from the Media Library and from the configured storage provider.

bearerAuth.description: Either an API token, created in the admin panel under Settings > API Tokens, or a JWT issued by the Users & Permissions plugin. Routes must also be enabled for the calling role under Settings > Roles; a route that is not enabled returns 403 even with a valid token. Public routes may be called without a token if the Public role permits them.

ApiId.name: apiId
ApiId.description: The API ID of the content type. Use the **plural** API ID for a collection type (e.g. `articles`, `products`) or the **singular** API ID for a single type (e.g. `homepage`). This is defined per instance by whoever modelled the content types.

ApiIdPlural.name: apiId
ApiIdPlural.description: The plural API ID of a collection type, e.g. `articles`. Single types have no per-document routes.

DocumentId.name: documentId
DocumentId.description: The document's `documentId`. This is the Strapi 5 identifier for a document; it is not the numeric `id` returned alongside it.

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description: Sort order. A field name optionally suffixed with `:asc` (default) or `:desc`, e.g. `sort=createdAt:desc`. Sort by several fields with indexed syntax: `sort[0]=title:asc&sort[1]=createdAt:desc`.

Filters.name: filters
Filters.description:
Filter the result set, using the syntax `filters[field][$operator]=value`, e.g. `filters[slug][$eq]=hello-world`.

Operators: `$eq`, `$eqi`, `$ne`, `$nei`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$notIn`, `$contains`, `$notContains`, `$containsi`, `$notContainsi`, `$startsWith`, `$startsWithi`, `$endsWith`, `$endsWithi`, `$null`, `$notNull`, `$between`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`.

Multiple fields are combined with `$and` implicitly. Relations can be traversed: `filters[author][name][$eq]=Kai`. Array values use indexed syntax: `filters[id][$in][0]=3&filters[id][$in][1]=6`.

Populate.name: populate
Populate.description:
Relations, components, dynamic zones and media to include. Relations are **not** returned unless populated.

Use `populate=*` for all first-level relations, a field name for one relation, indexed syntax for several (`populate[0]=author&populate[1]=categories`), or nested objects for deeper population (`populate[author][populate][0]=avatar`).

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description: Restrict the returned attributes, e.g. `fields[0]=title&fields[1]=slug`. `documentId` and `id` are always returned.

Pagination.name: pagination

pageSize.description: Documents per page, for page-based pagination.

start.description: Number of documents to skip, for offset-based pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return, for offset-based pagination.

withCount.description: Whether to run the count query and return totals in `meta.pagination`.

Pagination.description:
Pagination, e.g. `pagination[page]=2&pagination[pageSize]=50`.

The two pagination styles **cannot be mixed**: use either `page` with `pageSize`, or `start` with `limit`.

Status.name: status
Status.description:
Selects the draft or the published version. Omitting it is equivalent to `published`. Drafts have `publishedAt: null`.

Only meaningful when Draft & Publish is enabled for the content type. See the Draft & Publish caveats in the API description before relying on this parameter for create or update.

Locale.name: locale
Locale.description: Locale code of the version to operate on, e.g. `en` or `fr-FR`. Only meaningful when the Internationalization (i18n) plugin is enabled and the content type is localized.

PublicationFilter.name: publicationFilter
PublicationFilter.description: Selects documents by how their draft and published versions relate to each other — for example to find documents whose draft differs from what is currently published. See the Strapi documentation for the accepted values, which vary by version.

BadRequest.description: Bad request — typically a validation failure or an invalid query parameter.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized — the token is missing, malformed or expired.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden — the token is valid but the route is not enabled for its role under Settings > Roles.

NotFound.description: Not found — no such content type, document or locale.

Document.description: A Strapi document. Beyond the fields below, a document carries whatever attributes were modelled for its content type; these appear directly on the object. In Strapi 4 they were nested under `attributes`, which was removed in Strapi 5.

id.description: Numeric id of the underlying database row. Retained for backwards compatibility; use `documentId` to address the document.

documentId.description: Identifier of the document across all of its locales and draft/published versions. This is the identifier used by all collection-type routes.

publishedAt.description: When the document was published. `null` for a draft, which is the reliable way to tell a draft from a published document.

locale.description: Locale of this version. Present when the i18n plugin is enabled.

DocumentRequest.description: Request payload for creating or updating a document. Attributes go inside `data` and are specific to the content type being written.

data.description: The attributes to write. Relations are set by passing the related `documentId` (or an array of them). Media fields are set by passing the numeric file `id` returned by the Upload plugin.

DocumentResponse.description: Envelope returned for a single document.

DocumentListResponse.description: Envelope returned for a list of documents.

Pagination.description: Pagination metadata. Page-based requests return `page`, `pageSize`, `pageCount` and `total`; offset-based requests return `start`, `limit` and `total`. `total` and `pageCount` are omitted when `pagination[withCount]=false`.

UploadFile.description: A file in the Media Library. Note that media routes and media relations are keyed by the numeric `id`, not by `documentId`.

id.description: Numeric id. This is the value to pass when setting a media field on a document.

formats.description: Generated responsive variants for images, keyed by name — typically `thumbnail`, `small`, `medium` and `large`. Which are generated depends on the source dimensions.

ext.description: File extension, including the leading dot.

url.description: Public URL. Relative to the instance origin for local storage; absolute when an upload provider such as S3 or Cloudinary is configured.

provider.description: Upload provider that stored the file, e.g. `local`.

details.description: Error-specific detail. For validation failures this carries the offending fields.
